europe-protests.title: Youth protests continue across Europe, in places turning into riots and clashes
europe-protests.summary: A new wave of youth protests swept across several European countries, and in some places they escalated into clashes with police, arson and riots. In France, according to various reports, some actions remained largely peaceful, but violence and arrests occurred at individual rallies: media outlets write of hundreds and even more than a thousand detainees, as well as an investigation into attacks on security forces. Separate reports mention unrest in Germany, clashes in Portugal, and say the weekend protests affected seven European countries. In France, student school blockades are reportedly due to resume on Monday.

us-midterms.title: As the U.S. elections approach, intraparty splits, court disputes and forecasts about Trump’s power intensify
us-midterms.summary: In the United States, internal party conflicts intensified ahead of the midterm elections, especially in the key Senate race in Michigan. Democrat Haley Stevens, who lost the primary to Abdul El-Sayed, backed Republican Mike Rogers, drawing sharp criticism and deepening a split in the party. Against this backdrop, Reuters reports a legal setback for Republicans in Alaska, while other outlets write about Donald Trump’s visits to Iowa and Kansas and disputes over the court agenda. Several publications also say that the election results and the future of Trump’s power remain in focus.

ukraine-oleshky.title: In Ukraine, after the end of the ceasefire in Kherson region, attacks on energy infrastructure and evacuations resume
ukraine-oleshky.summary: After the ceasefire in Kherson region ended, Russia carried out strikes that left thousands of people in Ukraine without power. Reuters and the BBC write that the shelling coincided with the end of a rare humanitarian ceasefire that allowed civilians to be evacuated from occupied Oleshky. Ukrainian authorities, according to reports, continue to evacuate civilians from parts of Kherson region. Other reports also say that intense attacks continue on the front line, including in the Pokrovsk direction.

iran-hormuz.title: Two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz amid de-escalation talks
iran-hormuz.summary: Two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters and Iranian sources report, with one described as a supertanker. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the vessels “exploded” after striking mines, while a maritime agency separately reported a damaged vessel in the strait. Against this backdrop, reports also mention de-escalation talks and the fact that the strait remains unsafe for commercial shipping. Several outlets link the incident to the broader threat of a new escalation between the United States, Israel and Iran.

france-police-protests.title: In France and neighboring countries, new protests and investigations follow clashes with police
france-police-protests.summary: In France, an investigation has been opened into attempted murder over attacks with incendiary mixtures against security forces after the protests. AFP, Al Jazeera and other outlets write that after clashes in Paris and other cities, security personnel were injured, but suspects in the episode have not yet been identified. The Guardian adds that protests involving young people ended in street violence and also affected Germany, Switzerland, Portugal and Albania. It is separately reported that high arrest figures have continued amid the broader wave of demonstrations across the country.

israel-election.title: Israel’s political deadlock persists as disputes over the election and legitimacy deepen
israel-election.summary: Israel remains in a political deadlock after the election, and President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with party leaders on forming a new government. Media reports say the head of the election commission insists that the investigation into possible irregularities must not cast doubt on the outcome of the vote. Likud, according to reports, speaks of a “dark cloud” over the result until the review is completed, while opponents accuse the party of trying to delegitimize the outcome. On the streets, as the media write, division also persists: some demand a coalition, others reject the participation of Arab parties.

sports-misc.title: In world sport: titles, records and high-profile victories in football, running and tennis
sports-misc.summary: In world sport on this day, football, the marathon and wrestling stood out. Arsenal beat Liverpool at Anfield for the first time since 2012 and moved to the top of the Premier League table; different outlets described the match differently, but agree that the London side took the win and three points. Reuters also reports Real Madrid’s 3-0 victory over Racing Santander and the success of Athletic and Real Sociedad, who marked a memorable derby 50 years later. In the United States, Sheila Chepkirui won the New York marathon, while in Russian football Lokomotiv lost at home to Spartak 0-4. Reuters also reports the Raiders’ 38-33 win over the Jets, ending a losing streak.

binance-hack.title: Binance resumes withdrawals after record $6.3 billion crypto theft
binance-hack.summary: Crypto exchange Binance has resumed withdrawals after a hack in which, according to reports, more than $6.3 billion was stolen. Reuters, AFP, the BBC and other outlets write that the company said it had covered 90% of the losses and restored the platform to operation, although users were actively withdrawing funds in the first hours after reopening. The FBI, according to reports, blamed the attack on a North Korean group. This is one of the largest known crypto hacks.

The outlets agree that the strikes hit different areas of Gaza, including Gaza City and Khan Younis. The new casualties are being reported amid the continuing conflict and earlier destruction.

TASS reports that Gyurov has conceded defeat and also gives figures showing Yotova in the lead after part of the protocols were processed. india-protest.title: In India, the opposition again demands the resignation of the election chief over voter rolls
india-protest.summary: In New Delhi, India’s opposition again took to the streets in mass protests, demanding the resignation of the election commission chief over the revision of voter rolls. Reuters writes that thousands took part in the action, while other outlets report tens of thousands of demonstrators and leaders from different parties. The trigger remains a nationwide review of the voter lists, which the opposition sees as unfair and favorable to the ruling party. The protests have been going on since summer, and demonstrators once again raised the issue in the capital.

Reuters, AFP, NBC and Al Jazeera write that the FSB received information through partner channels and then detained the teenager, who is suspected of threatening an attack on a park. The project was part of tests of the conditions of long space travel and life in a confined space. It is one of the stages of preparation for a real mission to Mars.

golden-ivory-chess-piece.title: 18th-century ivory chess piece sells at auction for huge sum
golden-ivory-chess-piece.summary: An ivory chess piece found in a family drawer sold at auction for £735,000. It is reported that the piece had spent more than 55 years in the drawer and was identified as part of the Lewis chessmen. The report emphasizes the item’s rarity and historical value. It is a notable antiques sale.
golden-ivory-chess-piece.picture: The image shows an old ivory chess piece on velvet fabric. The scene highlights the value of the ancient object and its museum-level rarity.

ten-year-old-wildlife-fundraiser.title: 12-year-old London boy raises money for wildlife protection and earns Attenborough’s praise
ten-year-old-wildlife-fundraiser.summary: A 12-year-old boy from London raised £13,000 for wildlife protection and received praise from David Attenborough. The fundraising effort is reported to have won broad recognition. No other details about the campaign are given in the report. It is a short, positive story about charity.

alcaraz-wins-vienna.title: Carlos Alcaraz wins tennis tournament in Vienna
alcaraz-wins-vienna.summary: Carlos Alcaraz won the Vienna Open, maintaining a perfect run in the ATP 500 series. BBC reports that in the final he beat Alex de Minaur in straight sets. The victory extended his winning streak and strengthened his status as one of the tour leaders. It is another title in the Spaniard’s successful season.
alcaraz-wins-vienna.picture: The image shows a tennis player lifting a trophy above his head. It symbolizes victory and another title at the tournament.

articles.title: Alcaraz wins Vienna Open to maintain perfect record

dart-first-wta-title.title: Harriet Dart wins a WTA title for the first time in her career
dart-first-wta-title.summary: Harriet Dart won a WTA title for the first time in her career, triumphing at the Guangzhou Open. BBC and The Guardian report that the Briton came through qualifying and claimed her first WTA singles trophy at the age of 30. In the final she beat Lilli Tagger, coming back after losing the first set. For Dart, this is the biggest success of her career.
dart-first-wta-title.picture: The image shows a tennis player holding the winner’s cup. The picture marks her first title and an important personal breakthrough.

new-york-marathon-debut-win.title: Andreas Almgren wins the New York Marathon on his debut
new-york-marathon-debut-win.summary: Andreas Almgren won the New York Marathon on his debut over the distance. BBC reports that the Swede did it in his first attempt at the classic marathon distance. The Guardian separately reports that Sheila Chepkirui won the women’s race, reclaiming the title. For Almgren, it was a striking debut and the main result of the year.
new-york-marathon-debut-win.picture: The image shows a runner crossing the finish line. It is an image of an unexpected and important marathon victory.

arsenal-win-at-anfield.title: Arsenal win at Anfield for the first time since 2012
arsenal-win-at-anfield.summary: Arsenal won at Anfield for the first time since 2012 and moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League table. BBC and The Guardian report that the winning goal came from an early burst by Kai Havertz, while Liverpool were unable to respond. Other versions note that the match was tense and left the home side frustrated. It is an important victory in the race for the lead.
arsenal-win-at-anfield.picture: The image shows a ball lying in front of the goal. It represents the decisive moment of the match and a rare away win at a difficult venue.

articles.title: Arsenal move clear at the top with a rare win at Liverpool

man-city-edge-london-city.title: Manchester City edge London City in a WSL match
man-city-edge-london-city.summary: Manchester City narrowly beat London City Lionesses in a Women’s Super League match. BBC reports that goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp secured the win. The report also says London City played well but failed to take their chances. The victory helped City stay in the race near the top of the table.
